text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Chief Justice Yong Pung How has made landmark ruling on corruption after acquitting horse owner Chan Wing Seng of bribing his jockeys.

- Thousands of depositors withdrew savings from the Philippines Monte de Piedad and Savings Bank, reopened by Singapore rescuer Keppel Group after being forced to close operations on April 23 due to liquidity problems.
- Tat Lee Bank is to beef up its shareholders' funds with proposed rights issue that will bring it below the Singapore $1.5 billion mark required by law.
- Strong liquidity from improving trade flows make the region's stock markets, including Singapore, increasingly attractive over the next six to 12 months, two research houses said.

- Indonesia's Sinar Mas group formally launched its offer for the takeover of ailing electronic goods distributor Amcol Holdings through Asia Food & Properties Ltd, which is valued at US$2.25 billion.
- A two percent correction on Wall Street on Wednesday and a sharp upward spike in U.S. bond yields put the brakes on the local market's five day rally.
- Bre-X Minerals, the miner at the centre of the world's greatest gold hoax, has been delisted by the Toronto Stock Exchange and suspended by the Montreal and Alberta exchanges.
- John Felderhof, Bre-X Minerals chief of exploration, has taken refuge in the western Caribbean islands.
- The Philippines' powerful Catholic Church assured Keppel Group it would retain all its deposits with Keppel's recently acquired Monte de Peidad bank.
- Electronics company CAM International Holdings Ltd, whose two key directors are under a Commercial Affairs Department investigation, will use property sale proceeds to reduce bank borrowings.
- Yeo Hiap Seng will soft-launch The Sterling, its freehold condominium project in the Bukit Timah area, on Saturday an average net price of S$1,000 per sq ft.
